summary: Jackson County peak: camp 1918, cupola 1923, ODF cab 1963; cab torn down 2007-08, then a steel camera-detection tower in 2009 on a gated road.

facts.design: 14x14 ODF flattop cab with catwalk on a timber tower (1963)
facts.status_note: Cab torn down in 2007 or 2008 (sources differ). A steel camera-detection tower was flown in during 2009.

staffing.status: not staffed; staffed into the 2000s, then removed

access.note: A 1990 approval put a gate across the access road after an August request. The request said a regional communications agency needed only a key or lock to get through. No current source confirms whether the gate is still in use.

visit.trail_note: No lookout cab remains. The 2009 steel tower is a camera base, not a lookout, and is not a place to climb.

facts.agency: Oregon Department of Forestry, Southwest Oregon District

events.note: Camp set up as the first lookout on the site (tent or rag camp).
D-6 cupola cabin built on the summit.
Season's first lookout went on duty June 14, per a 1933 newspaper item.
Garage converted into an Aircraft Warning Service winter residence during World War II; site staffed year-round.
New ODF cab completed and old lookout removed. NHLR describes a 14x14 ODF flattop with catwalk on a timber tower.
Gate across Road No. 38-3-33 approved after thefts and vandalism.
Registered March 31, 2003, while the cab was still standing.
December 2006 fire burned part of a radio building at the base of the tower; the lookout itself was not burned.
Oregon chapter surveyed the lookout for fire damage from vandals and planned a new steel tower for spring 2008.
firelookout.com says destroyed after an arsonist damaged the structure; FFLOS says removed in 2007.
Oregon lookouts page says the structure was torn down, with debris hauled and burned.
Steel tower flown in by helicopter as a base for a camera detection system.

corrections.why: D-6 is the style the Oregon lookouts page gives for the 1923 cupola house. NHLR describes the 1963 cab as an ODF flattop with catwalk on a timber tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and firelookout.com date the loss to 2007 (FLO adds an arsonist). The Oregon lookouts page dates the tear-down to 2008 and says the debris was burned. Both years are recorded. The 2007 chapter report had planned a steel tower for 2008; the only later steel tower found is the 2009 camera base, and no source ties the two.
NHLR (2003) says the cab remains in active service, which was true at registration. Later registers and pages record its loss in 2007 and 2008.
NHLR gives 4,929 ft (1,502 m); FFLOS gives 5,023 ft (1,531 m). The record's 1502.4 m matches NHLR.
NHLR gives a 10-foot treated timber tower; FFLOS gives a 15-foot timber tower. Not recorded as a fact because the sources disagree.

notes_for_editor: Post-2007 history rests mainly on one Oregon lookouts page (the 2008 tear-down and 2009 steel camera tower), which is not independently confirmed. The 2007 chapter report planned a 20-foot steel tower for 2008; no source ties that plan to the 2009 tower. Access is recorded as restricted only from a 1990 gate letter; no current access source was found. Design correction: the record's D-6 belongs to the 1923 cupola. Many 1930s-1960s staffing details, the 1946 lightning strike and the 1990 break-ins are on the Oregon lookouts page and were not used in the story. Elevation and tower height disagree between NHLR and FFLOS. No WebSearch was available for this tower after the workflow budget ran out, so the fate and 2009 steel tower could not be checked elsewhere.
